chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Ali ibn Hadid, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: Al-mubarāh (divorce by mutual agreement) is a final divorce, and there is no revocation (raj'ah) in any of that. And Zurarah said: It does not occur except in the same state as the place of divorce, either when pure (from menses) or pregnant, with witnesses.

key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Revocation of divorce during the waiting period

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Mubarāh divorce in Shia fiqh and does it allow for revocation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies that 'al-mubarāh' is a distinct, irrevocable divorce (bā'in) where the husband forfeits the right of unilateral revocation (raj'ah) during the 'iddah, distinguishing it from the standard talaq. Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim further specify the procedural conditions, requiring the wife to be in a state of purity (tuhr) or pregnancy, with witnesses present, ensuring legal clarity in Shia jurisprudence.
